title: hardware-comparison-cloud-skus-cuda-drivers
summary: Investigation comparing inference performance across NVIDIA A100, H100, and NVIDIA L40S cloud SKUs, and across CUDA/driver versions. Goal: establish SKU/driver recommendations for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments and identify bottlenecks for our runtime optimizations.
content:
Background:
We were asked to produce an apples-to-apples comparison of common cloud GPU SKUs (A100, H100, L40S) across multiple cloud vendors and driver/CUDA versions used by customers. Focus is inference latency and steady-state throughput for our serving runtime with representative LLMs (70B dense and 13B decoder-only). Tests target 1) p99 token latency for single-request low-concurrency workloads, 2) tokens/sec at steady-state under high concurrency, and 3) GPU utilization and memory behavior to identify bottlenecks (memory bandwidth, kernel launch overhead, PCIe/NVLink effects).

Testbed and methodology:
- Models: 13B decoder-only (fp16), 70B dense (bfloat16 where supported). Both from our vetted model catalog with identical tokenizer and prompt sets.
- Runtime: internal serving runtime v0.19.3 with continuous batching disabled for single-request tests and enabled for throughput tests.
- Batching config: adaptive-batching for throughput with max-batch=64, max-latency-ms=30.
- Clients: 64 worker clients for concurrency tests, each issuing streaming generation with temperature=0.2, max_new_tokens=256.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, inference-seconds-per-token (cost proxy), GPU util (SM%), GPU memory usage, PCIe throughput, NVLink usage (where available).
- SKUs tested (cloud labels):
  - A100 80GB (g5a.12x / a100-80gb)
  - H100 80GB PCIe (h100-pcie-80gb) and H100 SXM (h100-sxm-80gb) where cloud provides
  - L40S 48GB (l40s-48gb)
- CUDA/driver matrix: CUDA 11.8 driver 525.x, CUDA 12.1 driver 535.x, CUDA 12.2 driver 540.x (when supported by the vendor SKU). Also included vendor-recommended patched drivers for H100 in some regions.
- Repeats: each test repeated 5 times at different times of day; outliers removed using 95% trimmed mean.
- Notes on fairness: firmware and microcode were left as provided by the vendor except where we explicitly tested NVLink-enabled SXM variants. For multi-instance SKUs we pinned processes to single GPU to avoid noisy neighbors.

Key findings (short):
1) H100 SXM > H100 PCIe > A100 > L40S for raw throughput on 70B when NVLink/SXM is available; advantage largely driven by H100 TF32+tensor core improvements and improved sustained memory bandwidth on SXM.
2) For 13B single-request latency, A100 and L40S were competitive; H100 shows improvements primarily for long-context workloads (>=2048 tokens) and large batch sizes.
3) CUDA/driver matters: moving from CUDA 11.8->12.1 gave systematic 5-12% tokens/sec improvements on H100 and A100 for our kernel mixes; CUDA 12.2 produced smaller incremental gains but introduced instability on some vendor images (observed occasional kernel failures on a patched H100 image - tracked in JIRA-INF-512).
4) Bottlenecks differ by SKU and workload: small model / low-latency workloads are kernel-launch and PCIe-limited on PCIe SKUs; large model / throughput workloads are compute- and memory-bandwidth bound, benefiting most from SXM NVLink and improved interconnect.

Detailed results (representative trimmed-mean values):
- 13B model (single-request, max_new_tokens=256, no batching):
  - A100 80GB (CUDA 11.8): p50 token latency 11.3ms, p95 18.4ms, p99 24.2ms, tokens/sec (streaming) ~86
  - H100 PCIe (CUDA 12.1): p50 10.2ms, p95 16.5ms, p99 21.7ms, tokens/sec ~93
  - L40S (CUDA 11.8): p50 11.6ms, p95 19.1ms, p99 26.0ms, tokens/sec ~82
Notes: variance for p99 is sensitive to PCIe transfers and driver scheduling.

- 70B model (throughput test, adaptive-batching, steady-state):
  - A100 80GB (CUDA 11.8): tokens/sec 3200, GPU util 78%, mem used 56GB
  - H100 PCIe (CUDA 12.1): tokens/sec 4300, GPU util 83%, mem used 60GB
  - H100 SXM (CUDA 12.1, NVLink): tokens/sec 5800, GPU util 92%, mem used 58GB
  - L40S (CUDA 11.8): tokens/sec 2900, GPU util 66%, mem used 45GB
Notes: H100 SXM sustain much higher throughput because of inter-GPU NVLink (for multi-GPU model partition experiments) and higher sustained tensor-core throughput for our workload; H100 PCIe still offers significant uplift vs A100 for this model. L40S falls behind for 70B as expected due to lower memory capacity and lower BFLOAT throughput for this model format.

Driver/CUDA observations:
- Upgrading to CUDA 12.1 on H100 consistently improved throughput by ~8-12% for our fused attention+kv-cache kernels.
- On A100 there were modest improvements (4-7%) moving to 12.1 but in some older vendor images the newer driver increased memory fragmentation leading to slightly higher peak mem usage.
- CUDA 12.2 showed improvements in small-kernel latency (helpful for low-latency 13B workloads) but had intermittent compatibility issues on certain cloud images (reproduce in one region on H100 PCIe; tracking in JIRA-INF-512).

Profiling notes and identified bottlenecks:
- Kernel timeline (nsight/cupti sampling) shows frequent short kernels for token-by-token decode in 13B. Kernel launch overhead and PCIe round-trip for small transfers are significant contributors to p99. Potential mitigations: continuous background batching, persistent kernel techniques, and more aggressive NVTX tracing to identify stragglers.
- For 70B multi-GPU runs, NVLink saturation correlates with step-time improvements; on SXM variants the interconnect is not saturated as early as PCIe variants, allowing better scaling across partitions.
- Memory bandwidth: A100 vs H100 shows H100 sustained bandwidth advantage; this aligns with higher tokens/sec for memory-bound attention kernels.
- SM Utilization: lower on L40S for 70B, indicating either compute under-utilization or that kernels are memory bound in the L40S HW path. We observed lower L40S bfloat/FP16 throughput for fused kernels compared to H100.

Operational considerations and reproducibility:
- Cloud SKU labels vary. We recommend standardizing our internal SKU tags and capturing driver and CUDA versions as part of deployment manifests.
- For Dedicated offerings, recommend H100 SXM where customers need max throughput for very large models (70B+) and have multi-GPU partitioning needs. For single-GPU latency-sensitive 13B workloads, A100 and L40S are cost-effective alternatives; L40S can be a lower-cost option but watch memory limits and BFLOAT kernel performance.
- Driver strategy: default to vendor-recommended stable CUDA 12.1 where available. Evaluate CUDA 12.2 experimentally in staging images but do not roll to production until JIRA issues closed. Maintain a driver compatibility matrix in the release notes for private deployments.

Action items / next steps:
- [Evan] Run additional A/B in-region tests to confirm the CUDA 12.2 instability is region-specific (JIRA-INF-512).
- [Maya] Produce lightweight deployment manifests that pin driver/CUDA versions for Dedicated and Private images; include checksum of driver package.
- [Jonah] Implement a short experiment for "persistent kernel" decode for 13B to reduce kernel launch overhead and measure p99 impact (target >20% reduction in p99).
- Add the full raw logs and perf traces to Confluence page linked above and attach compressed nsight timelines for 3 representative runs (70B SXM, 70B PCIe, 13B single-gpu).

Appendix (notes & caveats):
- These numbers are valid for our runtime v0.19.3 and the model builds used. Different tokenization, prompt lengths, or model operator fusions (custom kernels) will change absolute numbers but relative trends (H100 > A100 > L40S for large models) are stable across our sample.
- Some vendor images include additional telemetry and background agents that can affect p99; where possible we used minimal images.
- Cost implications: H100 SXM gives best tokens/sec but has a higher hourly cost; recommend adding a cost-per-million-tokens estimate to inform customer-facing SKU guidance (follow-up item).

If you want, I can attach the full CSVs and the raw nsight traces to this doc or create a short slide deck summarizing vendor recommendations for Sales/BD.
